title.narrative: Support for USAID and the Global Partnership for Assistive Technology in Grant Management and Operations

description.narrative:
Over one billion people need at least one form of assistive technology (AT), such as wheelchairs, eyeglasses, hearing aids, prosthetics, and personal assistance devices. 

By 2030, this number is expected to grow to more than two billion people. Today, over 90% of this population does not have access to the AT they need, creating significant consequences for individuals, their families, and society at large. Without AT, individuals may experience isolation and exclusion from education, the labor market, and civic life. Lack of access to appropriate AT causes poorer health outcomes including premature death, deteriorating mental health, and increased risk of chronic health conditions and secondary complications, all of which lead to a higher burden on health systems. Furthermore, there is a direct correlation between poverty and disability -- each one exacerbating and magnifying the other.

USAID is supporting ATscale, the Global Partnership for Assistive Technology to address the
enormous challenge. ATscale is an early stage cross-sector partnership that brings new energy and strategic focus to a significant, overlooked global challenge. ATscale's focus population are people who have a loss of function due to disability, aging, non-communicable diseases, injury or other causes who live in low and middle-income countries. USAID supports ATscale's focus on market building and the identification of new partners, such as the private sector, to AT. 

USAID is partnering with UNOPS to implement grant management and support operations to address this need.
